basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. VI.—Vers. 2.) Videntes autem filii Dei filias hominum, quia bonae sunt. Verbum'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. VI.—Vers. 2.) Videntes autem filii Dei filias hominum, quia bonae sunt. Verbum Hebraicum ELOIM (אלהים), communis est numeri: et Deus quippe et dii similiter appellantur: propter quod Aquila plurali numero, filios deorum ausus est dicere: Deos intelligens, Sanctos, sive Angelos. Deus enim stetit in synagoga deorum: in medio autem deos discernit. [Al. dijudicat] (Psal. LXXXI, 1). Unde et Symmachus istiusmodi sensum sequens, ait: Videntes filii potentium filias hominum, et reliqua.
